format: H264 Baseline / AAC / MP4, fast start
narration: Synthetic narration using the system Samantha voice; this is an evidence guide, not a claim of a new live AWS deployment.
provenance: Original captured evidence images and excerpts from the original live EKS recording. AWS resources were destroyed after capture.

chapters.title: Scientific calculator and saved notebook
chapters.narration: Orbit is a Python scientific calculator. Here it calculates and saves results to PostgreSQL.

chapters.title: Degree mode and persistent notebook
chapters.narration: Degree mode returns sine of thirty as zero point five. The shared notebook persists calculations.

chapters.title: 69 passing backend tests
chapters.narration: Sixty nine backend tests pass using isolated databases. Ruff also passes.

chapters.title: Meaningful version history
chapters.narration: More than ten meaningful commits, with secrets and generated files excluded.

chapters.title: Three healthy Compose services
chapters.narration: Compose runs three healthy services: frontend, backend, and PostgreSQL.

chapters.title: Non-root container users
chapters.narration: Both application containers run as non-root users. The frontend uses a multi-stage build.

chapters.title: Successful GitHub Actions pipeline
chapters.narration: GitHub Actions passes tests, builds, security scans, container publication, and a real cluster check.

chapters.title: Backend published with commit SHA
chapters.narration: Backend images are published to GitHub Container Registry with exact commit SHA tags.

chapters.title: Frontend published with commit SHA
chapters.narration: The frontend has matching immutable SHA tags, rather than a moving latest tag.

chapters.title: Backend image security result
chapters.narration: Trivy finds no high or critical vulnerabilities in the backend image.

chapters.title: Frontend image security result
chapters.narration: The frontend scan also passes. Either scan can block publication.

chapters.title: Real non-empty Terraform plan
chapters.narration: Terraform plans twenty real resources in Mumbai, including the VPC and EKS.

chapters.title: Terraform apply completed
chapters.narration: Apply completes successfully: twenty resources added. These are original captured results.

chapters.title: AWS Console · project VPC
chapters.narration: The AWS Console shows the provisioned project VPC in ap-south-one.

chapters.title: AWS Console · two public subnets
chapters.narration: Two public subnets span separate availability zones.

chapters.title: AWS Console · active EKS cluster
chapters.narration: The EKS control plane is active in the same region.

chapters.title: AWS Console · two Ready workers
chapters.narration: Two worker nodes are Ready. This is the actual captured EKS Console.

chapters.title: Helm releases on real EKS
chapters.narration: Helm manages the application, Ingress controller, and monitoring releases on EKS.

chapters.title: Application pods are Running
chapters.narration: Two backend and two frontend replicas are Running, alongside PostgreSQL.

chapters.title: ClusterIP Services
chapters.narration: ClusterIP Services expose both application tiers inside Kubernetes.

chapters.title: Ingress routing
chapters.narration: Ingress routes the root to the frontend, and API requests to FastAPI.

chapters.title: Backend Prometheus metrics
chapters.narration: The metrics endpoint exposes real Prometheus request and latency measurements.

chapters.title: Both application targets are UP
chapters.narration: Prometheus scrapes both backend replicas. Both targets are UP.

chapters.title: Populated Grafana dashboard
chapters.narration: Grafana displays populated live request, latency, and error panels.

chapters.title: Actual rollout and persistent notebook
chapters.narration: After the successful pipeline, a local Helm upgrade deploys the exact published commit.

chapters.title: Notebook survives the deployment
chapters.narration: The health endpoint reports that commit, and the saved notebook survives pod replacement.

chapters.title: Terraform destroy completed
chapters.narration: Terraform destroy removes the remaining resources. AWS evidence is historical; the infrastructure is now deleted.

chapters.title: Independent AWS cleanup audit
chapters.narration: An independent audit confirms no project cluster, VPC, volumes, or active workers remain.

chapters.narration: Temporary credentials are removed. README links all screenshots, source logs, and the original live recording.
